steps.body: Ordering a whole list just repeats the comparison rule over and over. Sort roughly by digit count first — that separates most of the list instantly. Then, for any numbers sharing the same digit count, compare place by place to break the tie.
Align two large numbers before deciding which comes first.

choices.feedback: One million has seven digits; 987,654 has six. The seven-digit number is greater.
The leading 9 looks large only after alignment. A seven-digit number is greater than any six-digit number.

choices.label: They are equal
choices.feedback: The numbers have different digit counts, so they cannot be equal.

widget.successFeedback: 1,000,000 is greater because it has one more place. Check digit count before comparing leading digits.
widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the place-value stages before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the aligned place-value model and the highlighted place.

predict.prompt: Comparing two big numbers — what do you check FIRST: digit COUNT or leading digits?
predict.reveal: More digits means a higher place is occupied — a 6-digit number beats every 5-digit one before a single digit is read. Length first; digits break the ties.

explanationVariants: 62,400 and 62,900 share the same 5 digits; the hundreds place (4 vs 9) shows 62,400 is smaller, so it comes first when ordering least to greatest.
Comparing place by place, 62,400 is the smaller of the two.

widget.prompt: Ordering least to greatest, which comes FIRST: 62,900 or 62,400?

options.feedback: Both have 5 digits; the hundreds place (4 vs 9) shows 62,400 is smaller, so it's first.
62,900's hundreds digit (9) is bigger than 62,400's (4), making 62,900 the LARGER number — it comes second, not first.

options.label: They're tied
options.feedback: They share the same digit count but differ at the hundreds place (4 vs 9) — not a tie. 62,400 is smaller.

options.label: Can't tell without more digits
options.feedback: The hundreds place alone already decides it: 62,400 is smaller than 62,900.

steps.body: Ordering **greatest to least** uses the exact same rule, just read backward: the number that would come LAST in a least-to-greatest list comes FIRST here. Nothing new to learn — just flip the direction.

explanationVariants: Reading the least-to-greatest order backward (450,000, 45,300, 45,000, 6,000), 450,000 is greatest and 45,300 is second-greatest.
Flip the least-to-greatest list: 450,000 is greatest, 45,300 is second.

widget.prompt: Among 450,000, 6,000, 45,300, and 45,000 — which is the SECOND-greatest?

options.feedback: Greatest to least: 450,000, then 45,300, then 45,000, then 6,000. Second-greatest is 45,300.
450,000 is the GREATEST (most digits). The second-greatest is the next one down: 45,300.
45,000 is third-greatest — it's smaller than 45,300 at the hundreds place. Second-greatest is 45,300.
6,000 is the smallest of the four (fewest digits). Second-greatest is 45,300.

widget.prompt: Ashville: 'six hundred four thousand, twelve.' Bridgeton: 604,102. Cedar Falls: 89,999. Dunmore: 604,001. Order the towns from LEAST to GREATEST population.

misorderFeedback.feedback: Ashville (604,012) and Dunmore (604,001) share the same digits until the tens place — Dunmore's tens digit (0) is smaller than Ashville's (1), so Dunmore comes first.

widget.missFeedback: Convert Ashville's word form first (604,012), then sort: Cedar Falls has fewer digits; the other three tie at 6 digits and need place-by-place comparison.
widget.successFeedback: Cedar Falls (89,999, fewer digits) is least; among the three 604,0xx numbers, the tens and hundreds places break the tie: Dunmore, then Ashville, then Bridgeton.

explanationVariants: Bridgeton (604,102) is greatest and Cedar Falls (89,999) is least; 604,102 − 89,999 = 514,103.
Subtracting the least from the greatest gives 514,103.

widget.prompt: What is the difference between the greatest population (Bridgeton, 604,102) and the least population (Cedar Falls, 89,999)?

commonErrors.feedback: 604,102 is just Bridgeton's population alone. Subtract Cedar Falls' 89,999 from it: 604,102 − 89,999 = 514,103.
515,103 is off by exactly 1,000 — recheck the borrow through the thousands and hundreds columns. The true difference is 514,103.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Subtract the least population from the greatest: 604,102 − 89,999.

hints: Convert Elmsworth's word form first: 'six hundred four thousand fifty' is 604,050.
Elmsworth joins Ashville (604,012), Bridgeton (604,102), and Dunmore (604,001) — all four share the same leading digits.
Compare the hundreds and tens places carefully among all four close numbers, then place Cedar Falls (89,999) as the smallest overall.
explanationVariants: Full order least to greatest: Cedar Falls (89,999), Dunmore (604,001), Ashville (604,012), Elmsworth (604,050), Bridgeton (604,102). Elmsworth ranks 4th out of 5.
Elmsworth's 604,050 slots in between Ashville's 604,012 and Bridgeton's 604,102, making it 4th from least.

widget.prompt: A fifth town, Elmsworth, has a population of 'six hundred four thousand fifty.' Ordering all five towns (Ashville, Bridgeton, Cedar Falls, Dunmore, Elmsworth) from least to greatest population, what RANK does Elmsworth hold (1st = least)?

commonErrors.feedback: 3rd would be Ashville (604,012). Elmsworth's 604,050 is bigger than Ashville's at the tens place (5 vs 1), placing Elmsworth one rank higher: 4th.
5th (greatest) is actually Bridgeton (604,102), whose hundreds digit (1) beats Elmsworth's (0). Elmsworth ranks just below it: 4th.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Convert Elmsworth to standard form (604,050), then compare it against all four other towns place by place.

takeaways: Ordering repeats comparison: sort by digit count first, then break ties place by place.
Greatest-to-least uses the identical rule, just read in reverse.
Close numbers sharing many leading digits still separate cleanly once you reach their first difference.
steps.teaser: That's every skill Place Value to a Million set out to teach — the ×10 ladder, reading and writing big numbers, rounding any place, adding and subtracting with regrouping, and now comparing and ordering. On to the next Grade 4 trail.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Sort by digit count first, then break ties place by place.** For 82, 900, and 75: 82 and 75 have 2 digits, 900 has 3 — so 900 is biggest. Between 82 and 75, the tens place (8 vs 7) shows 82 is bigger. Order least to greatest: 75, 82, 900.

explanationVariants: 900 has 3 digits, more than either 82 or 75 — it's the greatest.
Digit count alone makes 900 the biggest of the three.

options.feedback: 900 has 3 digits; the others have only 2. More digits wins.
82 has only 2 digits. 900 has 3, making it the greatest.
75 has only 2 digits and is also smaller than 82. 900 (3 digits) is the greatest.
